packages.title: Calculus Investigation Starter
packages.subject: Calculus
packages.summary: A clarity-first scaffold for investigating functions, derivatives, critical points, convexity, and definite integrals with exact bounded examples.
packages.details: This starter helps an instructor build a calculus Class around rational-coefficient polynomials on bounded rational intervals. It supplies explicit language, notation, examples, nonexamples, and a deterministic investigation palette while leaving course identity, sequencing, Study binding, and publication policy to the instructor.

packages.title: Linear Algebra Investigation Starter
packages.subject: Linear Algebra
packages.summary: An exact finite-matrix scaffold connecting rank, nullity, determinant, trace, symmetry, and invertibility through bounded investigations.
packages.details: This starter helps an instructor build a linear algebra Class around small integer matrices interpreted over the rational numbers. Definitions distinguish matrix representations from linear maps, examples expose complete calculations, and the investigation palette remains bounded and deterministic.

packages.title: Combinatorics Investigation Starter
packages.subject: Combinatorics
packages.summary: A finite-permutation scaffold for exploring fixed points, inversions, descents, derangements, and parity through exact enumeration.
packages.details: This starter helps an instructor build a combinatorics Class around permutations of finite labeled sets. It emphasizes exact definitions and hand-checkable examples before students use bounded enumeration to form and refute conjectures.

packages.title: Graph Theory Investigation Starter
packages.subject: Graph Theory
packages.summary: A finite-simple-graph scaffold for investigating connectivity, bipartiteness, trees, degree, clique number, and chromatic number.
packages.details: This starter helps an instructor build a graph theory Class around finite simple graphs. It separates definitions that students often conflate, provides hand-checkable examples and boundary cases, and exposes a bounded deterministic palette that can resolve against an exact Graph Theory Study revision.
